    public function isReference(Tokens $tokens, int $index): bool
    {
        if ($tokens[$index]->isGivenKind(CT::T_RETURN_REF)) {
            return true;
        }

        if (!$tokens[$index]->equals('&')) {
            return false;
        }

        /** @var int $index */
        $index = $tokens->getPrevMeaningfulToken($index);
        if ($tokens[$index]->equalsAny(['=', [T_AS], [T_CALLABLE], [T_DOUBLE_ARROW], [CT::T_ARRAY_TYPEHINT]])) {
            return true;
        }

        if ($tokens[$index]->isGivenKind(T_STRING)) {
            $index = $tokens->getPrevMeaningfulToken($index);
        }

        return $tokens[$index]->equalsAny(['(', ',', [T_NS_SEPARATOR], [CT::T_NULLABLE_TYPE]]);
    }
}

    // intersection/union types in fn params
    '<?php $f = fn (A&B $x, A|B $y) => $x;',
];

part.text:
Fixed in src/Tokenizer/TokensAnalyzer.php: `isUnaryPredecessorOperator` didn't recognize arrow functions (`T_FN`), so `&` reference parameters inside `fn(...)` fell through to `isBinaryOperator` and got spaced by `binary_operator_spaces`.

The fix:
1. Added `[T_FN]` to the probe token list so the nearest preceding `fn` keyword is found.
2. Added a `T_FN` handling block: if the `&` lies within the arrow function's parameter list, it's a reference (unary predecessor); if it lies in the body after `=>`, it remains binary.

Verified:
- The issue case no longer changes (`string &$property` stays intact), even nested inside method bodies.
- Binary `&` in arrow fn bodies (`fn ($a, $b) => $a&$b`) is still correctly spaced, as are `fn &()`, untyped `&$a` params, intersection types, and regular functions/closures.
- `tests/Tokenizer` (1891 tests) and `tests/Fixer/Operator` (1323 tests) pass; the full suite shows only 4 pre-existing environment-related failures (smoke/phar/IO tests), confirmed present before the change.
